ground_truth.mechanism: The layer-2 (always-ask) checks in command_tool_checks only send tools that are on the name list (Monitor), so if always_ask_match went back to `tool in COMMAND_TOOLS`, which ignores the arguments, no check would fail; an unknown tool carrying a command line such as FutureShell {command: 'git push --force origin topic'} would then skip the always-ask rule and go to the reviewer under AUTO without asking the owner.

ground_truth.mechanism: command_text joins every command-key value into one string with newlines before any layer judges it, so an unclosed quote or a trailing backslash in one field carries into the next field's text: a DENY command that another field holds (for example `sudo rm -rf /` or `pkill -f daemon2`) is read as a quoted argument or a continued `echo`, so layer 1 does not refuse it and layer 4's static_verdict can ALLOW it with no card for a human-backed asker.

ground_truth.mechanism: Adding run_readonly to V2_COMMAND_TOOLS sends a fast-path desk run_readonly call through v1_request as run_command. The v2 permit now checks it against run_command allowlist entries instead of run_readonly ones. Existing {"tool":"run_readonly","prefix":...} entries stop covering it, so the owner is asked again. A run_command entry now covers it, and an Always on a run_readonly card writes a run_command stem entry that also auto-allows that stem in the full shell. None of this is mentioned in the 2026-10-15 safety note or tested.

ground_truth.mechanism: When a command arrives as an argv array, `_command_value` joins its items with plain spaces instead of shell-quoting them (`shlex.join`). So `['bash','-lc','pkill -f daemon2']` turns into `bash -lc pkill -f daemon2`. The rules then treat only `pkill` as the `-c` payload and read `-f daemon2` as `$0`/`$1`, so the layer-1 DENY that catches the quoted string form never fires. Under AUTO the call goes to the reviewer instead. The space join already existed in main's `_command_of`. Reach is narrow: Codex's paths pass the command as a string and decline anything that isn't one, and Claude's Bash sends strings. That leaves unknown or MCP tools that send an argv array, which this PR now routes into layer 1 through `is_command_tool`.

non_issues.claim: The Always-on-Monitor test only checks that some run_command allowlist entry exists, so it still passes if the entry is minted without its prefix and becomes a whole-tool grant.
non_issues.why_not: The assertion at line 2148 is loose, but it hides no defect. Under the current code a prefix-less run_command entry cannot be created. entry_for either returns {'tool': tool_name, 'prefix': stem} for a command tool or raises NotAllowlistable for an empty or compound command. The only way to get a prefix-less entry is to change entry_for itself, and the same suite's main() already runs lines 880-882, which pin the exact {'tool': 'run_command', 'prefix': 'pnpm'} entry. The reviewer admits those lines catch the mutation. The suite as a whole fails, so the guard is not left untested.
